newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia's biggest bank says stronger after job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Zambia's biggest bank says stronger after job cuts.

text.p: Zambia's biggest bank said on Tuesday it had shed 1,000 jobs in a restructuring programme needed to consolidate its market position.

"The bank has reduced staffing levels from 2,400 as at May 1995 to 1,400 as at today's date, representing a 42 percent reduction," Samuel Musonda, acting managing director of the state-run Zambia National Commercial Bank, told reporters.
"This exercise has been carried out as amicably as possible."

The bank embarked on a restructuring programme in 1995 following the collapse of three other commercial banks -- Meridien BIAO Bank Zambia, Commerce Bank and Africa Commercial Bank -- in the face of severe liquidity problems in 1994.
Musonda said that following the restructuring programme, which included the introduction of new technology systems, the bank was in a stronger position than before.
"The way forward is very bright. It is...clear that the rigorous, painful decisions taken during the year under review are already paying dividends," he said.
